# First physical step: 20 examples for stuck admin tasks

A first step is something you could see happen. Thirty examples, from a call to a form to a document, and how to check your own.

7 min read Updated 26 September 2026

In this guide 12 sections

A first physical step is something a person watching you could see happen, such as finding a phone number, opening a form or putting a letter on the desk. It isn't deciding, planning or thinking it over. Pick the task, then find the example below closest to it and copy its shape.

This is a reference list of thirty first steps for stuck admin: calls, forms, messages, mail and home jobs. It can't choose your task or tell you how urgent it is, and it isn't a substitute for professional support if being unable to start is affecting your health or work.

Image: A three-row table pairing a task with its first physical step, dentist, insurance claim and spare room, beside a note to pick one step for today.Example steps; copy the shape, not the task.

The task feels too big to start, so you plan it. Deciding is invisible, and it's the thing you're stuck on.
Find the policy letter and put it on the desk  | Yes. Someone watching sees it happen, and it takes a few minutes.

## Calls

The most common first step is not the call itself. It's the piece of information the call will ask for.

  * Book the dentist

The first physical step
    Look up the phone number and write it down

  * Make a doctor's appointment

The first physical step
    Find the phone number and the times you could go

  * Call the landlord

The first physical step
    Write what you'll say in one line

  * Chase a refund

The first physical step
    Find the reference number from the last contact

  * Deal with a bill dispute

The first physical step
    Find the statement showing the charge

  * Cancel a subscription

The first physical step
    Open the account page and find the cancel or manage option

  * Book a repair

The first physical step
    Take a photo of the problem

  * Call the school office

The first physical step
    Write your question on one line and put it next to the phone

Sign up for something with a cutoff  | Write the cutoff date on a sticky note where you'll see it

## Messages and replies

Writing the first line or one word is a real action. The polish comes later.

  * Answer a difficult email

The first physical step
    Write only the first line

  * Ask for help

The first physical step
    Send one message that says what you need

  * Reply to an invitation

The first physical step
    Type the one word, yes or no, in the reply box

  * Chase an email nobody answered

The first physical step
    Open the old message and note the date you sent it

  * Thank someone you never thanked

The first physical step
    Write one sentence saying what they did

Chase an email nobody answered  | Open the old message and note the date you sent it
Thank someone you never thanked  | Write one sentence saying what they did

## Home and clutter

Set up the job so the next step is obvious, before doing any of it.

  * Sort out the spare room

The first physical step
    Call the charity shop about collection

  * Sort the mail pile

The first physical step
    Open the top five items and do nothing else

  * Return to an old project

The first physical step
    Find where you left it and put it on the desk

  * Clear the kitchen counter

The first physical step
    Put one bin bag by the door

  * Fix a dripping tap

The first physical step
    Take a photo of the tap and find the brand name on it
